_contract: Authored by Tasklet 2026-08-16 directly to contract v3, mirroring the Boston exemplar (phase3/boston-fleet-investors.json) per GROK-SPEC-archetype-templates-2026-08-15.md + ADDENDUM v3. Sources: washington-dc/REVENUE-STACK-WASHINGTON-DC.md + CREW-COST-WASHINGTON-DC.md + SPEED-RULES-WASHINGTON-DC.md + washington-dc/hub.json (v2026-08-15-dc-mece-f3). CONTRACT v3: only `title` (≤6 words), `value`/figures, `note` (≤140 chars, partner-clean plain English), `status` (enum: market_priced | modeled | upside), and `fn` (footnote key) render — plus verbatim copy fields (headline/subline/body/chips/cards/quantity/price). Underscore-prefixed fields (_contract, _provenance, _internal, _guard) NEVER reach the DOM. null/missing = render nothing. Footnotes render ONCE in a single 'Notes & assumptions' section above the contact form. This is fleet financing only — the equity/fundraise/defense/Gulf content firewalls in FLEET-INVESTORS-BRIEF.md §5 apply in full. D6′ LOCKED: utilization-stack economics lead frame; self-own kill list applied. Upside rows are never summed into base totals. DC SPECIFICS: (1) seat band $750–1,000/seat-month is DERIVED from local premium benchmarks (fn6) — there is no DC price precedent in the program; (2) the conservative case does not cover operating costs — payback renders as a neutral '—' with fn7; (3) fleet_phasing is OMITTED — no sourced DC vessel counts or fleet plan exist this pass; nav anchor 'Plan' dropped accordingly; (4) the hub's 2019-shutdown daily-ridership figure and the Occoquan commuter-base figure are excluded (flagged unverified in research); (5) demand pool renders hub.json employer figures only — no capture-derived seat estimates, because DC has no tracker-stated capture input.

fn1.text: Pricing and experience rates are benchmarked to Washington-area operators' published 2025–26 fares.

fn2.text: Demand pool figures are indicative of demand potential along these corridors — not commitments or commercial relationships. Headcounts are planning estimates from public reporting.

fn3.text: Economics are indicative ranges with conservative defaults. Upside lines — sponsorship and overnight cargo — are never included in base totals.

fn4.text: All trip times respect posted harbor speed limits. Speed-rule relief appears only as a separately labeled upside, never in base cases. Precedent: an electric hydrofoil exemption on Stockholm's Route 89.

fn5.text: Crew costs are benchmarked to published Washington-area wage data with a buffer for wage growth to 2026; shift structure to be confirmed in an operations walkthrough.

fn6.text: The $750–1,000 seat-month band is derived from Washington benchmarks — walk-up water-taxi fares, premium commuter passes (VRE, OmniRide), rideshare and parking costs. It is a derived planning band, not an operating quote.

fn7.text: In the conservative case, revenue does not cover operating costs, so no payback figure is shown. The case appears for transparency, not as a plan.

fn_n30_exec.text: N30 executive economics are indicative platform figures (all-in cabin + F&B on a ~$1M vessel, one captain, fixed AM/PM slots plus wait buffer). Shoulder charters/experiences are additive. Not a quote — ops walkthrough required.

copy.headline: One asset. One day. Four demand layers.

upside_rows.note: Naming and station sponsorship, priced from transit-sponsorship precedents. Never summed into base totals.

Route-specific relief where wake and noise are independently measured. The District's code provides the mechanism; not quantified here.

navier_intro.title: Meet the vessel

copy.headline: A U.S.-built electric hydrofoil, not a boat with a battery.
copy.body: Navier is a U.S. builder of electric hydrofoil vessels. Its N45 Explorer carries 30 passengers at a foilborne cruise speed of about 30 knots — lifted clear of the chop for a smooth ride above the wake and wash of conventional boats. The smaller N30 Quanta carries 8. Foiling cuts energy use by up to ~90% versus a conventional planing hull, and both vessels run near-silent on electric power.

tech_chips.value: up to ~90% less than a planing hull

copy.note: A vessel is a network asset, not stranded in one market — the 7-city network is the residual-value story.

copy.headline: Dedicated executive slots — then fill the rest of the day.
copy.body: Employers are asking for Uber-shuttle privacy: fixed AM/PM departures for their people only, with a wait buffer, Wi‑Fi tables, and F&B all-in. One captain runs the boat and hospitality. Midday and evening charters still monetize the shoulder. Payback is on the ~$1M N30 — not the N45 workhorse.
